questions.q: Choose the sentence with correct subject-verb agreement.
o: The list of items are on the desk.
The list of items is on the desk.
The lists of item is on the desk.
The list of items were on the desk.
questions.e: The subject is the singular noun 'list', so the verb must be singular: 'is'. 'Of items' is only a modifier.

questions.q: Fill in the blank: She ____ to the office every day by bus.
questions.e: A habitual action with a singular third-person subject takes the simple present with -s: 'goes'.

questions.q: Fill in the blank: They ____ their project yesterday.
questions.e: 'Yesterday' marks a finished past action, so the simple past 'completed' is correct.

questions.q: Choose the correct article: He is ____ honest engineer.
questions.e: 'Honest' begins with a vowel sound (the h is silent), so it takes 'an'.

questions.q: Choose the correct preposition: The meeting is scheduled ____ Monday.
questions.e: Days of the week take the preposition 'on'.

questions.q: Choose the correct pronoun: The manager gave the report to Priya and ____.
questions.e: After the preposition 'to' we need an object pronoun: 'me'.

questions.q: Which sentence is written correctly?
o: Their going to submit the form today.
There going to submit the form today.
They're going to submit the form today.
Theyre going to submit the form today.
questions.e: 'They're' is the contraction of 'they are'. 'Their' shows possession and 'there' shows place.

questions.q: Choose the word closest in meaning to 'rapid'.
questions.e: 'Rapid' means happening at great speed, which is the same as 'quick'.

questions.q: Choose the word opposite in meaning to 'expand'.
questions.e: 'Expand' means to become larger, so its opposite is 'shrink'.

questions.q: Choose the word closest in meaning to 'begin'.
questions.e: 'Begin' and 'start' both mean to take the first step in doing something.

questions.q: Fill in the blank: Please ____ the form carefully before you sign it.
questions.e: The base verb 'read' fits after 'please'. 'Red' is a colour and 'reed' is a plant.

questions.q: Choose the word opposite in meaning to 'ancient'.
questions.e: 'Ancient' means very old, so the opposite is 'modern'.

questions.q: Which is the most suitable opening for a formal email to a person you have not met?
questions.e: A formal email to someone you do not know should open with a respectful greeting such as 'Dear Mr. Rao,'.

questions.q: Which closing is most appropriate for a formal email?
questions.e: 'Yours sincerely' is a standard, polite closing for formal correspondence.

questions.q: A teammate asks you for the status of your task. Which reply is clearest?
o: The module is 80% done; testing will finish by Thursday.
questions.e: A good status update is specific: it states progress and gives a clear deadline.

questions.q: Passage: 'Riya reviews code every morning before meetings begin. She says it keeps her mind sharp and helps her catch bugs early.' When does Riya review code?
questions.e: The passage says she reviews code 'every morning before meetings begin'.

questions.q: Passage: 'The library closes at 8 p.m. on weekdays but stays open until 5 p.m. on Saturdays. It is closed on Sundays.' On which day is the library NOT open?
questions.e: The passage states the library is closed on Sundays.

questions.q: Choose the correct plural of 'analysis'.
questions.e: Nouns ending in -is form the plural with -es: 'analyses'.

questions.q: Choose the correct sentence.
questions.e: After 'doesn't' the main verb stays in its base form: 'doesn't like'.

questions.q: Fill in the blank: I have lived in Hyderabad ____ 2019.
questions.e: 'Since' is used with a specific starting point in time such as a year; 'for' is used with a duration.

questions.q: Identify the error: 'Each of the students have submitted their assignment.'
questions.e: 'Each' is singular, so the verb should be 'has submitted'.

questions.q: Choose the correct sentence.
o: Neither the manager nor the engineers was present.
Neither the manager nor the engineers were present.
Neither the manager nor the engineers is present.
Neither the manager nor the engineers has been present.
questions.e: With 'neither...nor', the verb agrees with the nearer subject. 'Engineers' is plural, so 'were' is correct.

questions.q: Choose the best replacement for the underlined part: 'If I would have known about the delay, I would have left earlier.'
questions.e: A third conditional (past unreal) uses 'had + past participle' in the if-clause: 'If I had known'.

questions.q: Choose the sentence with correct punctuation.
o: Its a long road, but it's worth it.
It's a long road, but its worth it.
It's a long road, but it's worth it.
Its a long road, but its worth it.
questions.e: Both clauses mean 'it is', so both need the contraction 'it's'. 'Its' is the possessive form.

questions.q: Choose the correct sentence.
o: Having finished the report, the email was sent.
Having finished the report, she sent the email.
Having finished the report, the email she sent.
Having finished, the report the email was sent.
questions.e: The opening phrase must refer to the person who finished the report, so the main clause needs that person ('she') as the subject. The other options leave the phrase dangling.

questions.q: Choose the correct sentence.
o: She is more smarter than her brother.
She is smarter than her brother.
She is most smarter than her brother.
She is smart than her brother.
questions.e: The comparative of 'smart' is 'smarter'. Do not combine 'more' with an -er form.

questions.q: Convert to indirect speech: He said, 'I am learning Python.'
o: He said that he is learning Python.
He said that he was learning Python.
He said that I was learning Python.
He said that he has learned Python.
questions.e: In reported speech the present continuous shifts back to the past continuous, and the pronoun 'I' becomes 'he'.

questions.q: Choose the correct sentence.
o: The committee has announced it's decision.
The committee has announced its decision.
The committee have announced its' decision.
The committee has announced their's decision.
questions.e: 'Its' (no apostrophe) is the possessive. 'It's' means 'it is' and the other forms are not valid.

questions.q: Choose the word that best fits: 'The new policy was met with strong ____ from employees, who felt it was unfair.'
questions.e: Employees who feel a policy is unfair would push back, so 'resistance' fits the context.

questions.q: Choose the word closest in meaning to 'meticulous'.
questions.e: 'Meticulous' describes someone who pays great attention to detail.

questions.q: Choose the word opposite in meaning to 'scarce'.
questions.e: 'Scarce' means in short supply, so the opposite is 'abundant'.

questions.q: Choose the word closest in meaning to 'mitigate'.
questions.e: To mitigate something, such as a risk, is to make it less severe.

questions.q: Fill in the blank: The auditor found several ____ between the two financial reports.
questions.e: An auditor comparing reports looks for differences; 'discrepancies' means inconsistencies.

questions.q: Choose the word closest in meaning to 'concise'.
questions.e: 'Concise' means expressing much in few words.

questions.q: Choose the correct word: The new feature will ____ the performance of the app.
questions.e: 'Affect' is the verb meaning to influence. 'Effect' is usually a noun meaning result.

questions.q: What does the idiom 'to hit the nail on the head' mean?
questions.e: The idiom means to say or do something that is exactly correct.

questions.q: What does the phrase 'bottleneck' mean in a project context?
o: A point that slows down the overall process
questions.e: A bottleneck is a stage that limits throughput, like the narrow neck of a bottle.

questions.q: Your teammate's code has a bug. Which feedback is the most professional?
o: There is an off-by-one error in the loop on line 42; changing the bound to n-1 should fix it.
Why can't you ever get this right?
questions.e: Good feedback is specific, focuses on the work and suggests a fix, without criticising the person.

questions.q: You must decline a meeting because of a clash. Which reply is best?
o: I have a clash at that time and will not be able to attend. Could we move it to 3 p.m. or share the notes afterwards?
questions.e: A polite decline explains briefly and offers an alternative, keeping the relationship constructive.

questions.q: Which subject line is best for an email asking your manager to approve leave?
questions.e: A clear subject line states the purpose and key details so the reader knows what is needed.

questions.q: In a group discussion another participant makes a point you disagree with. What is the best approach?
o: Interrupt and say they are wrong
Stay silent for the whole discussion
Acknowledge their point, then present your view with a reason
questions.e: Respectful disagreement acknowledges the other view and supports your own with reasoning.

questions.q: Passage: 'Remote work has increased flexibility for many employees. However, some teams report weaker collaboration because spontaneous conversations happen less often.' What is the main idea?
o: Remote work is always better than office work
Remote work offers flexibility but can reduce spontaneous collaboration
questions.e: The passage presents both a benefit (flexibility) and a drawback (less spontaneous collaboration).

questions.q: Passage: 'Although the prototype passed all unit tests, it failed under real traffic because the tests used unrealistically small datasets.' Why did the prototype fail under real traffic?
o: The unit tests were not run
The tests did not reflect real data sizes
questions.e: The passage says the tests used unrealistically small datasets, so they missed problems that appear at real scale.

questions.q: Passage: 'Priya compared three vendors. Vendor A was cheapest but slow to deliver; Vendor B was costly but reliable; Vendor C balanced cost and speed.' Which vendor offers the best balance?
questions.e: The passage says Vendor C balanced cost and speed.

questions.q: Passage: 'The release was postponed twice, not because of code quality, but because the deployment checklist was incomplete.' What caused the postponements?
questions.e: The passage explicitly rules out code quality and names the incomplete checklist.

questions.q: Choose the sentence that uses the semicolon correctly.
o: I finished the report; and sent it.
I finished the report; it is in your inbox.
I finished; the report it is in your inbox.
I finished the report, it; is in your inbox.
questions.e: A semicolon joins two closely related independent clauses, as in 'I finished the report; it is in your inbox.'

questions.q: Identify the error: 'Not only did the system crash, but also it corrupted the database.'
o: Not only did the system crash
questions.e: After 'not only' the parallel clause should be inverted as well: 'but it also corrupted' or 'but also did it corrupt'. 'but also it corrupted' is not grammatical.

questions.q: Choose the sentence that is free of faulty parallelism.
o: She enjoys coding, to read blogs, and attending hackathons.
She enjoys coding, reading blogs, and attending hackathons.
She enjoys to code, reading blogs, and attend hackathons.
She enjoys coding, reading blogs, and to attend hackathons.
questions.e: Items in a list should share the same form. Coding, reading and attending are all gerunds.

questions.q: Choose the sentence with correct use of 'whom'.
o: Whom is responsible for the deployment?
The engineer whom I mentored has joined Google.
The person whom called you is waiting.
questions.e: 'Whom' is the object form. In 'whom I mentored', 'whom' is the object of 'mentored'. The other sentences need 'who' as the subject.

questions.q: Choose the sentence in which the modifier is placed correctly.
o: The manager only approved the budget on Friday.
The manager approved only the budget on Friday, not the hiring plan.
Only the manager approved on Friday, the budget being.
The manager approved on Friday the only budget.
questions.e: 'Only' should sit directly before the word it limits. Here it limits 'the budget', contrasting it with the hiring plan.

questions.q: Choose the correct sentence.
o: The reason is because the server ran out of memory.
The reason is that the server ran out of memory.
The reason is due because the server ran out of memory.
The reason being because the server ran out of memory.
questions.e: 'The reason is' should be followed by 'that', not 'because', since 'reason' and 'because' are redundant together.

questions.q: Choose the word that best completes the sentence: 'The architect's design was ____: it solved the problem with the fewest possible components.'
questions.e: Solving a problem with the fewest components describes an 'elegant' design. 'Convoluted' and 'redundant' mean the opposite.

questions.q: Choose the word closest in meaning to 'ubiquitous'.
questions.e: 'Ubiquitous' means seeming to be everywhere at the same time.

questions.q: Choose the word closest in meaning to 'ambiguous'.
o: Open to more than one interpretation
questions.e: An ambiguous statement can reasonably be understood in more than one way.

questions.q: Choose the word opposite in meaning to 'verbose'.
questions.e: 'Verbose' means using more words than needed, so the opposite is 'succinct'.

questions.q: In the sentence 'The startup's growth was meteoric', what does 'meteoric' suggest?
questions.e: Like a meteor streaking across the sky, 'meteoric' growth is very rapid.

questions.q: A client is upset about a missed deadline. Which response is the most professional?
o: It's not our fault; your requirements kept changing.
We apologise for the delay. The release is now planned for Friday, and we will update you daily until it ships.
questions.e: An effective response takes responsibility, gives a concrete new plan and sets expectations for follow-up.

questions.q: You need to explain a technical outage to a non-technical executive. Which summary is best?
o: A race condition in the connection pool caused deadlocks across replicas.
Some users could not log in for 40 minutes because of a software fault. It is fixed, and we are adding checks to prevent a repeat.
Everything is broken but we are on it.
The outage was caused by engineers.
questions.e: Tailor to the audience: state impact, duration, current status and prevention in plain language.

questions.q: Passage: 'Automation reduces repetitive work, but it does not remove the need for judgment. Teams that automate without monitoring often discover errors only after customers do.' Which statement is best supported?
o: Automation needs human monitoring to be reliable
Judgment is unnecessary once tasks are automated
questions.e: The passage warns that automation without monitoring leads to late discovery of errors, implying monitoring is required.

questions.q: Passage: 'The survey found that 70% of respondents preferred the new interface. However, only 120 of the 10,000 users were surveyed.' What is the main limitation of the finding?
o: The sample is very small relative to the user base
questions.e: Only 1.2% of users were surveyed, so the result may not represent all users.

questions.q: Passage: 'Critics argue that strict code-review rules slow delivery. Proponents counter that the time saved by avoiding production bugs outweighs the delay.' What does the author present?
o: Two opposing views on code-review rules
A conclusion that reviews are useless
questions.e: The passage describes what critics say and what proponents say in response, without taking a side.

questions.q: Passage: 'The pilot succeeded in one city, so the company assumed it would succeed nationwide. Within a quarter, it had closed half of its new branches.' What flaw in reasoning does the passage illustrate?
questions.e: The company assumed a result from one city would hold everywhere, which is a hasty generalisation.
